rationale: Empirical review at artifact commit 694b9d46 passes the R4 lens. The three AC-8(i) real-bd/real-git variants all succeeded and verified the notice, in_progress claim state, and bead worktree creation for an untracked file, an untracked directory tree, and a modified tracked file. AC-8(ii)'s real-claim enumeration pin passed. AC-8(iii)'s seam injection classified only the injected entangled path as blocking and routed it through the preserved DirtyTreeFailure invariants while leaving unrelated dirt out of the refusal. A separately hand-driven claim in a disposable /tmp repository emitted the required one-line stderr notice naming operator-notes.txt, returned exit 0, and left the bead in_progress; the installed bd independently refused worktree creation under the world-writable /tmp ancestry and emitted its existing recovery warning, so actual successful worktree creation is established by the three isolated integration fixtures rather than that manual /tmp leg. All five AC-16 dispositions passed: absent phase writes plan with honest backfill output, same-value plan performs zero writes with honest no-op output, and implement/review/done each remain untouched with zero writes. The reviewed worktree remained byte-identical and all scratch fixtures were cleaned.

findings.summary: All three AC-8(i) real claim variants proceed with notice and create worktrees.
findings.evidence: go test ./cmd/mindspec -run '^TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_(UnrelatedDirtVariantsProceedWithNotice|EnumerationPin)$' -count=1 -v -timeout 30m passed. Subtests untracked_file, untracked_directory_tree, and modified_tracked_file passed; their assertions require claim success, a notice naming the dirty path, status in_progress, and existence of the new bead worktree. The real-claim enumeration pin also passed.

findings.summary: A hand-driven /tmp claim names unrelated dirt, claims successfully, and exits zero.
findings.evidence: In a disposable real Git+bd fixture, with untracked operator-notes.txt in the invoking checkout, the reviewed binary emitted as stderr line 1: 'note: claiming despite unrelated dirty path(s) this claim does not touch (not blocked — ADR-0025 R5.1): operator-notes.txt'; the command exit was 0 and bd show reported the bead status in_progress. Current bd then rejected its worktree-create subprocess because BEADS_DIR was beneath world-writable /tmp and emitted the pre-existing recovery warning. This is fixture-environment behavior, not a reviewed-code failure; the three Go integration fixtures above independently establish successful worktree creation.

findings.summary: Seam-injected entanglement re-arms refusal through the preserved DirtyTreeFailure contract.
findings.evidence: TestCheckDirtyTreeProportional_InjectedEntanglementBlocks passed. With entangled.txt injected and both entangled.txt and unrelated.txt dirty, blockingDirt was exactly [entangled.txt], ignoredDirt exactly [unrelated.txt], and DirtyTreeFailure satisfied the shared contract invariants, named entangled.txt, and omitted unrelated.txt. The reviewed diff contains no changed DirtyTreeFailure contract lines.

findings.summary: All AC-16 replay/backfill legs pass with mutation honesty.
findings.evidence: The targeted internal/approve run passed EmptyStoredPhaseBackfillsPlan, SameValuePlanReplayIsNoOp, and LaterPhaseReplayLeavesItUntouched with implement, review, and done subtests. The tests assert exactly one plan write for absent metadata, zero writes for plan/implement/review/done, backfill wording only on the mutation path, and stored-phase naming on no-op paths.

findings.summary: Build, artifact identity, byte integrity, and scratch cleanup passed.
findings.evidence: make build completed; targeted tests all passed; HEAD remained 694b9d46e9f1f85e4e44a3143859b098548acce6; git diff, git diff --cached, and git status --porcelain were empty; both disposable /tmp fixture roots were deleted.
